react_result.final_narrative_text: Multi-paradigm enrichment of nine differentially abundant metabolites reveals convergent perturbation of sulfur-amino-acid metabolism and biopterin-dependent pathways, with a strong oxidative/xenobiotic signal. RaMP ORA (FDR 0.00165) identified L-cysteine (KEGG:C00097), coumarin (C05851), and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid (C00632) as the primary drivers of 'Metabolism' (REACT:R-HSA-1430728) and 'Biological oxidations' (REACT:R-HSA-211859). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently ranked Thiamine metabolism (hsa00730, p=0.013), Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism (hsa00430, p=0.015), Pantothenate and CoA biosynthesis (hsa00770, p=0.037), One carbon pool by folate (hsa00670, p=0.048), and Glutathione metabolism (hsa00480, p=0.052) — all driven by L-cysteine as the sole input hit. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis placed Dihydrobiopterin (C02953) and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid at the center of Tyrosine metabolism (rank 0, p=0.0044), Biopterin metabolism (rank 1, p=0.010), and Tryptophan metabolism (rank 2, p=0.010). 3-Hydroxyanthranilic acid additionally anchors the RaMP ADHD and autism (ASD) pathways (WP:WP5420) and Reactome 'Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives' (R-HSA-71291). Coumarin drives the xenobiotics metabolism signal in Mummichog (rank 3, p=0.036). The co-enrichment of L-cysteine across cysteine/methionine, glutathione, and CoA biosynthesis pathways, coupled with elevation of 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid and dihydrobiopterin in tryptophan/tyrosine biopterin branches, suggests systemic oxidative stress and altered one-carbon metabolism as the dominant biological theme, consistent with combined chemical-exposure and redox-imbalance phenotypes.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three enrichment tools produced convergent results across ORA and m/z-direct paradigms. RaMP multi-DB ORA returned ten pathways at FDR=0.00165, with L-cysteine and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid as the sole hits for Metabolism, ADHD and autism (ASD) pathways, and Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives, while coumarin and L-cysteine co-hit Biological oxidations. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis identified Tyrosine metabolism (p=0.0042, 4 hits) and Biopterin metabolism (p=0.0092, 3 hits) as top network-matched pathways; dihydrobiopterin (C02953) was the sole input hit for Biopterin metabolism and co-hit Tryptophan metabolism alongside 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirmed Thiamine metabolism (hsa00730, p=0.013) and Taurine and hypotaurine metabolism (hsa00430, p=0.015), both driven by L-cysteine. L-cysteine and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid are the primary drivers of the amino acid and metabolism cluster; dihydrobiopterin and 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid co-drive the biopterin-tryptophan branch; L-cysteine and coumarin co-drive biological oxidations. 3-hydroxyanthranilic acid does not participate in biological oxidations, establishing pathway exclusivity for the drivers. The convergent signal across tools implicates perturbed amino acid metabolism with a secondary biopterin/tryptophan branch.
